title: Aspect Deep 5: Phase Verbs Take Imperfective Infinitives
titleRussian: Виды глагола 5: Фазовые глаголы и инфинитив
description: Verbs that mark the start, continuation, or end of an action (начать, продолжать, закончить, перестать, бросить, стать) take ONLY an imperfective infinitive.
descriptionRussian: Глаголы, обозначающие начало, продолжение или конец действия (начать, продолжать, закончить, перестать, бросить, стать), требуют только инфинитива несовершенного вида.
intro: Here the choice stops being a choice. Verbs that mark the beginning, continuation or end of an activity take an imperfective infinitive and nothing else, no matter what you mean. The reason is that the phase verb has already supplied the boundary, so the infinitive is only there to name the activity. One of the few places in aspect where you can stop thinking.
rules: Phase verbs (начать, начинать, продолжать, закончить, перестать, бросить, стать) take ONLY an imperfective infinitive: 'начал читать,' 'закончил писать,' 'продолжает учить.'
The reason: the phase verb already marks where the action begins, continues, or ends. The infinitive describes the activity itself, which is process by nature.
The phase-verb construction reports a phase change in the activity. To report a completed RESULT, use the perfective verb directly: 'Я написал статью' rather than 'Я закончил писать статью.'
The rule applies regardless of the phase verb's own aspect. Both 'начал читать' (pf phase verb + impf inf) and 'начинает читать' (impf phase verb + impf inf) are correct.
examples: Маша начала читать роман. (Masha started reading the novel.) Начать + impf inf.
Антон закончил писать статью в полночь. (Anton finished writing the article at midnight.) Закончить + impf inf.
Они продолжают учить русский язык. (They keep studying Russian.) Продолжать + impf inf.
Я перестал пить кофе вечером. (I (m) stopped drinking coffee in the evening.) Перестать + impf inf.
Лена бросила играть в шахматы. (Lena gave up playing chess.) Бросить + impf inf.
Маша стала читать больше. (Masha started reading more.) Стать + impf inf.

items.promptEnglish: Drink water every day; it's good for you.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 4: каждый день frames the command as what?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4: каждый день is a frequency cue and frames the command as a habit. Imperfective imperative: Пей. Today's lesson moves to the infinitive position after phase verbs, where the rule is even sharper: only the imperfective is allowed.

items.promptEnglish: Masha started reading a long novel yesterday.
items.hint: Phase verb 'начать' takes which aspect of infinitive?
items.explanation: Phase verbs take ONLY an imperfective infinitive. Начать + читать. The perfective прочитать is ungrammatical here, no matter how 'completed' the eventual reading might be. The phase verb provides the temporal edge; the infinitive provides the activity, which is impf.

items.promptEnglish: Anton finished writing the article around midnight.
items.hint: Phase verb 'закончить' takes which infinitive aspect?
items.explanation: Закончить is a phase verb meaning 'to finish doing.' Like all phase verbs, it takes the imperfective infinitive: закончил писать. The perfective написать would claim a result and clash with the phase verb's role of marking the activity's end.

items.prompt: Они продолжают _____ русский язык каждый день.
items.promptEnglish: They keep studying Russian every day.
items.explanation: Продолжать is a phase verb of continuation: it requires an imperfective infinitive. Продолжают + учить. The perfective выучить would claim a completed result, which the open-ended 'keep studying' meaning rules out.

items.promptEnglish: I (m) stopped drinking coffee in the evening.
items.explanation: Перестать is a phase verb of ending: it requires an imperfective infinitive. Перестал + пить. The perfective выпить would mean 'drink up in one go,' which makes no sense after 'stopped.'

items.promptEnglish: Anton gave up studying English a year ago.
items.hint: Phase verb 'бросить' (give up doing) takes which infinitive?
items.explanation: Бросить in this sense means 'gave up doing' and is a phase verb of ending. It requires an imperfective infinitive: бросил + учить. The perfective выучить would mean 'master / learn through,' which contradicts giving up.

blanks: Маша стала чаще _____ длинные книги. (Masha started reading long books more often.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Стать in this sense ('to start doing more often') is a phase verb of beginning. Phase verbs take an imperfective infinitive: стала + читать. The frequency cue 'чаще' reinforces the habitual reading. The perfective прочитать would claim a single completed reading, which 'started reading more often' rules out.

minimalPairs.explanation: Phase verb начать takes only an imperfective infinitive: начала читать. The perfective прочитать is ungrammatical after a phase verb.

Phase verb закончить takes only an imperfective infinitive: закончил писать. To say the article is done with the result claimed, Russian uses the bare perfective: 'Антон написал статью.' The two constructions answer different questions.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha started watching a new series.
errorCorrection.explanation: Phase verbs take ONLY an imperfective infinitive, so начала смотреть. The perfective посмотреть cannot follow a phase verb: начать already supplies the temporal edge (the start), and the infinitive just names the ongoing activity.

Закончить is a phase verb of ending and takes an imperfective infinitive: закончил рисовать. The perfective нарисовать would claim the picture's result, which the bare perfective already says on its own: нарисовал картину.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я перестал съесть сладкое по вечерам.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I stopped eating sweets in the evenings.
errorCorrection.explanation: Перестать is a phase verb of ending and takes an imperfective infinitive: перестал есть. The perfective съесть means 'eat up in one go', a single completed act, which cannot follow 'stopped': you stop an ongoing habit, not a completed bite.

errorCorrection.sentence: Они продолжают спеть в хоре каждую неделю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: They keep singing in the choir every week.
errorCorrection.explanation: Продолжать is a phase verb of continuation and takes an imperfective infinitive: продолжают петь. The perfective спеть means 'sing through to the end once', which contradicts the open-ended 'keep singing every week'.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждый раз Антон начинает приготовить ужин слишком поздно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Every time, Anton starts cooking dinner too late.
errorCorrection.explanation: Начинать is a phase verb of beginning, and every phase verb takes an imperfective infinitive: начинает готовить. The perfective приготовить ('cook to a finished result') cannot follow начинать, which marks only the onset of the activity. The rule holds whether the phase verb is perfective (начал) or imperfective (начинает).

errorCorrection.sentence: В новой школе дети стали изучить два языка.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: At the new school, the children started studying two languages.
errorCorrection.explanation: Стать in the sense 'began, took up' is a phase verb of beginning and takes an imperfective infinitive: стали изучать. The perfective изучить ('study through to mastery') claims a result, which clashes with стать's job of marking only the onset of the activity. To report the result, use the bare perfective: 'дети изучили два языка' (they mastered two languages).

errorCorrection.sentence: После перерыва студенты продолжили решить задачи.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: After the break, the students continued solving the problems.
errorCorrection.explanation: Продолжить (the perfective continuation verb) takes an imperfective infinitive, exactly like its imperfective partner продолжать: продолжили решать. The perfective решить ('solve to a result') clashes with the continuation meaning, which is open-ended process. This shows the rule holds no matter the phase verb's own aspect, perfective or imperfective.

reviewVocab.definition: phase verb (a verb that marks the beginning, continuation, or end of an action; takes an imperfective infinitive without exception)
reviewVocab.example: Фазовые глаголы (начать, продолжать, закончить) сочетаются только с инфинитивом НСВ.

reviewVocab.definition: to continue (imperfective phase verb of continuation; followed by an imperfective infinitive: 'продолжаю учить русский')
to stop doing (perfective phase verb of ending; followed by an imperfective infinitive: 'перестал пить кофе')
